evidence.section: 3.5 Analysis of alloy composition using d-electron approach
evidence.quote: The Al 10 Hf 25 Nb 5Sc 10 Ti 25 Zr 25 alloy with Bo ≈ 2.87 and Md ≈ 2.49 values locates under the Ms=RT line, to the right from the Mf=RT line. ... Thus, it can be suggested that the Bo-Md diagram is an adequate tool for predicting the structure and deformation mode of the Al 10 Hf 25 Nb 5Sc 10 Ti 25 Zr 25 alloy.

Room temperature tensile strength testing was carried out to determine the deformation mode of the Al 10 Hf 25 Nb 5Sc 10 Ti 25 Zr 25 alloy. The stress–strain plots for the as-cast state (continuous line) and after annealing at 1000°C for 5 h (dashed curve) are shown in Fig. 15a. An evident difference in the behavior of the as-cast and annealed Al 10 Hf 25 Nb 5Sc 10 Ti 25 Zr 25 alloy is observed. For the as-cast state, an average tensile strength reaching 900 MPa, (continuous curve) is accompanied by the strain of 4.2 %, while the yield strength and hardness amount to 500 MPa and 390 HV, respectively. Annealing leads to significant increase of the tensile strength, reaching up to 1240 MPa, while the yield strength and plasticity increase to 660 MPa and 11.5%, respectively. The hardness of the sample increases to 485 HV.

The as-cast Al 10 Hf 25 Nb 5Sc 10 Ti 25 Zr 25 sample during the uniaxial compression tests (Fig. 15b) showed a dual-yielding effect with the “primary” yield point of 620 MPa, fracture strength of 2132 MPa, and the overall plastic strain of 20%.
After the annealing of the sample, it revealed 1940 MPa at the yield strength of 1168 MPa.
The hardness of the as-cast and subsequently annealed alloy increase to 520 HV and 540 HV for the samples elongated by ε = 4.2% and 11.5%, respectively.

The alloy in the as-cast state consists of large grains with size up to 1000 mm within bcc cell dendritic structure and dimensions of 20-40 µm. Very fine orthorhombic needle-like structure with thickness up to 50 nm and length reaching 1 µm is revealed within cell grains.

The Al10Hf25Nb5Sc10Ti25Zr25 at.% alloys were prepared from the elements of 99.99 wt.% purity in an arc melting furnace with a water-cooled copper plate and under protective Ar atmosphere. The high purity titanium was applied as the getter. In the applied technology, the solidification proceeds at the average cooling rate of about 100˚C/s. To ensure sufficient homogenization, the alloys were re-melted 5 times.

In addition, plates reveal increased concentration of Zr, Sc and Hf at the expense of Nb and Ti. They are located within bcc phase enriched in Nb and Ti.
The results suggest a bcc-to- α’ phase transformation during compression as well as twins formation.

The calculated difference between motionless lattice energies ∆E0 of the considered phases clearly indicates that the hcp A3 structure of the 5-component Al 15 Hf 25 Sc 10 Ti 25 Zr 25 at.% HEA is the most energetically stable at T = 0 K.
Above these temperatures the bcc A2 phases of both 5- and 6-component HEAs become energetically preferred.

Their morphologies are typical for the martensitic structures, which are presumably formed during the diffusionless transformation induced by rapid cooling (about 100˚C/s) just after arc melting.
